accuracy.evidence: The four structures and their signal words follow the CCSS RI.4.5 wording (chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) and the standard signal-word lists in Meyer's text-structure research. Every science fact in the passages was checked: Apollo 11 launched on 16 July 1969 and landed four days later on 20 July (NASA); sharks have skeletons of cartilage while most fish are bony fish; most owls are nocturnal and hawks diurnal; a honeybee worker emerges about 21 days after the egg is laid, after the larva spins a cocoon; bumblebees store only small amounts of honey; frogs have smooth moist skin and toads dry, warty skin (Britannica, RSPB, Bumblebee Conservation Trust).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers report for RI.4.5: labelling a structure from one signal word (the 'First, … However' trap passage and the prediction 'Yes, first means time order'), believing the topic fixes the structure (four bee passages each in a different structure, prediction 'Yes, each topic has its own', volcano challenge tag topic), reading events in the order written when 'because' puts the effect first (cause-chain step, schools-closed prediction, challenge tag mention), and blurring cause and effect with problem and solution (litter and compost passages, goal step).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtstr is the only lab about how non-fiction texts are organised: tapping signal-word phrases inside running text, sorting whole passages into four structures, fitting passages to a timeline, Venn diagram, cause arrow or problem box, rebuilding cause chains from effect-first sentences, and matching an author's goal to a structure. flagadvl (adverbials linking paragraphs), flagcohe (cohesion devices) and flagpic (pictures and text) use different mechanisms, and the 30% shingle gate passed against every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner works out each idea by doing it before it is stated: three paragraphs light up different signal words that end in a named structure, so signal words become clues; the bee step forces one topic into four organisers, so the author's choice decides the structure; the chain step only fills its cause slot when the because-clause event is tapped first, so written order and time order come apart; the done messages then name each rule.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, first means time order' before sorting the trap passage, 'Yes, each topic has its own' before the four bee passages, and 'Schools closed' for what happened first. The step right after each one tests that exact choice, and A.reveal quotes the learner's guess in the done message so they see whether it held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own reason: because and order (sharks text compares, nothing causes), compare and cause (which signal words fit which structure), mention and same (written first is not happened first), compare2 and order2 (a call to action needs problem and solution), topic and any (goal decides structure). Sorting slips name the clue, for example that 'First' only starts a list when 'However' sets two things side by side.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK 3.5, well inside the learner kid limit of 6.5, with one structure per sentence and concrete examples (frogs and toads, the flood). Adult text measures FK 9.0, inside the 9.5 limit, while using the precise terms text structure, chronological order, compare and contrast, cause and effect, problem and solution, signal or transition words, graphic organiser and author's purpose. Passages are two short sentences each.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and overlap with Cohesion within paragraphs, Linking paragraphs with adverbials and Pictures and Text Working Together stays under the 12% gate. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (the four plans, signal words, whole text not one word, author not topic) and each adult paragraph has one job: curriculum, key terms with organisers, named mistakes, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark: the signal-word paragraph steps its font down from 17 to 13 px until all lines clear the result box, the four structure boxes sit two by two at about 160 px each, cause-chain slots fit four across with short labels, the result line wraps inside its box, and every structure, organiser and event has a full-width button twin below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, and every Show me finished in time. Each canvas tap or drag has a labelled button twin (Time order, Venn diagram, Heavy rain, Unlike) and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'Chain built: Heavy rain, then The river rose, then Streets flooded, then Schools closed.'
